It is still ~-45% below its all-time high of ~18 months ago.

analyst_reports.business_description: The largest subscription streaming service in the world (over 137M global streaming members), five quarters past a self-inflicted debacle (bungled price restructuring + aborted spinoff of its legacy disc-rental segment) that cost it ~3.3M home-market subscribers and -75% of its market value. The recovery thesis has now printed twice: the entry-era recovery quarter ~3 quarters ago, and a just-reported quarter that beat on subscribers AND profit. The business model is deliberately two-speed: a profitable home-market streaming segment expanding margin ~100bps/quarter plus a melting-but-rich disc annuity, funding heavy international expansion (seven-country footprint spanning ~40 markets) and a new original-content slate.
recent_developments: The confirming print, ~1 week ago: +8.4M home-market streaming net adds (the debacle is now demonstrably behind it), a surprise GAAP profit where the street expected a loss, and home-market streaming contribution margin of 18.5% vs 10.9% a year ago. The stock closed +42% the next day — its biggest one-day gain ever — squeezing a ~13%-of-float short base.

~2 months ago: an exclusive multi-year output deal with THE major family-entertainment studio — first-run theatrical titles will stream exclusively on SMC in the premium pay-TV window starting with titles released three years out, displacing the premium cable incumbent that had held those rights for over a decade. It is the company's first premium-window output deal with a major studio in its home market; catalog and direct-to-video titles start immediately.

The company's flagship original series — a big-budget political drama from an A-list film director and A-list lead, all 13 episodes released simultaneously — premieres TODAY across every market. Management calls it 'a defining moment in the development of internet TV'; four more originals follow this year, including the revival of a cult comedy with a built-in fanbase.

An activist investor disclosed a ~10% stake a quarter ago (cost basis ~65% below the current price) and is publicly pushing for value maximization, including a possible sale to a larger technology or media acquirer.

Bear case, stated honestly: the stock has already tripled off its low; FCF is negative (-$209M last quarter, rescaled) and worsens next quarter as originals cash goes out the door, with a debt raise planned; the disc annuity (50% margins) is melting; the giant e-commerce rival is spending aggressively on its bundled streaming service and just launched its own original pilots; the premium cable incumbent's streaming app keeps expanding; and per-subscriber content obligations keep ratcheting up (~$10B rescaled on the balance sheet).

Competitive-overlap datapoint from management: of the service's 200 most-watched titles, 113 appear on none of the three rival streaming services in its home market; management argues the rivals are becoming different services, not substitutes, as everyone pivots to exclusives and originals.
analyst_reports.macro_context: Internet-connected TVs, tablets and game consoles continue to proliferate; the holiday quarter saw record device activations, directly feeding streaming sign-ups. Pay-TV cord-cutting is measurable but still early. Equity markets are risk-on; heavily-shorted recovery names are squeezing hard, which cuts both ways for entry timing.
